sentences.text: The petitioner herein has assailed the proceeding being C.S. Case No.90282 of 2023 under Sections 420/406 of the Indian Penal Code presently pending before the learned Judicial Magistrate, 19th Court, Calcutta.
It has been alleged in the complaint that the petitioner approached the opposite party for obtaining loan and induced him for granting loan of Rs.40,00,000/-.

The petitioner admittedly paid substantial portion of the loan amount but the petitioner has failed to repay of Rs.15,15,924/- till date in spite of several persuasions and thereby the petitioner has cheated the complainant.
Being aggrieved by the aforesaid proceeding, learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the present dispute over under-payment of the loan amount does not attract criminality.
He further submits that under the settled law proceeding under Sections 420/406 of the Indian Penal Code cannot run concurrently over the selfsame set of facts.

He further submits that from the averments of the complaint, it is clear that there was no deception at the inception as the petitioner admittedly paid substantial amount of loan and, therefore, allegation of cheating does not attract.

Furthermore,
since there was no entrustment, the allegation of criminal breach of trust has got no application in the present context.
Having heard learned counsel for the petitioner, the application is admitted.
Petitioner is directed to serve a copy of application upon the opposite party through speed post intimating the next date of hearing and to file affidavit-of-service on the returnable date.
Let the matter be listed in the monthly list of March, 2026 under the heading "Contested Application".
Learned counsel for the petitioner also prays for interim relief.

Having heard learned counsel for the petitioner and that the petitioner has made out an arguable case which requires to adjudication on merits, let the main proceeding being C.S. Case No.90282 of 2023 presently pending before the learned Judicial Magistrate, 19th Court, Calcutta is hereby stayed for a period of twelve weeks or until further order, whichever is earlier.
